question: The population of a town in the year 1921 was 3,47,900. If its population increased in two successive decades by 50% in each decade, the population of the town in the year 1941 was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial population = 3,47,900

Decade 1 increase = 50% → Multiplying factor = 1.5

Decade 2 increase = 50% → Multiplying factor = 1.5

Final population = 3,47,900 × 1.5 × 1.5 = 3,47,900 × 2.25

Calculation: 347900 × (9/4) = 86975 × 9 = 7,82,775

**∴ The correct answer is 7,82,775.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial population in 1921 = 3,47,900 | Time period = 1921 to 1941 (2 decades) | Growth rate = 50% per decade.

**Formula Used:** Final Population = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b1d86c7372acfcfc967f8f9a66c3b73c1769a638a812214b723cfc0a55d12f39.png] 

⇒ Population in 1931 = 3,47,900 + 50% of 3,47,900

⇒ Population in 1931 = 3,47,900 + 1,73,950 = 5,21,850

⇒ Population in 1941 = 5,21,850 + 50% of 5,21,850

⇒ Population in 1941 = 5,21,850 + 2,60,925

⇒ Population in 1941 = 7,82,775

**∴ The correct answer is 7,82,775.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

Compound Growth Formula

Population growth usually follows the compound interest formula: A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ where n is the number of time intervals.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

For quick calculation, 50% increase means multiplying the base value by (1 + 1/2) = 3/2 or 1.5.</p
